about: The scoped term-ruling set the AI-reviewed layer's gate reads (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-ai-layer-scaffolding-design.md, Unit B). Compiled by tools/ai-review/compile-ruling-set.js from `base` (the frozen 2026-10-11 set: its stage1 and before rows) and `exceptions` (scope exceptions to D2's book-wide default). Deterministic: a test recompiles it and requires byte equality, so never edit it by hand. One ruling per enNorm, after the base's supersededInBefore is applied (a superseded target survives only as a competitor). `id` is a slug of enNorm minted here. `en` lists every English form the rows carry, plus each form with its parentheticals removed (case kept). `is` is the recorded target, unchanged. `competitors` are the other renderings the rows name: a before row's competitor; a stage1 row's stored word, tied words, stored alternatives and superseded page answer; any superseded target; never the target itself (compared with every parenthetical removed, case ignored). `kinds` are the before kinds plus 'stage1'; `sources` cite each row. `scope` is {kind:'book'} with scopeStatus 'default' unless the exceptions file names the headword; a 'proposed' width is not ruled, and the gate admits no operation for it. `sense` is null unless the exceptions file restricts the ruling to one sense of a homograph: then {id, gloss, otherSenses, status}, the model names the sense it judged from that closed list or 'unclear', and the gate refuses an edit that does not declare `id` (a 'proposed' sense admits nothing). `matchable` is false, with codes in unmatchableReason, when the target holds a digit, a Greek letter, an uppercase letter after the first letter of a run of letters, an operator or bracket character, an underscore, or a non-ASCII space or control character, or when the enNorm holds a bracketed placeholder such as [formula]. Held rows and rows without a target are listed under `excluded`, never ruled. `amendments` is a dated input that carries out a decision record: it retargets, adds or removes a ruling, each entry citing the record and the decision. A retarget or a remove names the current target, so an amendment written against another set refuses; a retarget's old target survives as a competitor and the ruling gains kind 'amendment' and a source; an add mints a book-wide ruling of kind 'amendment'; a removed headword is listed under `excluded` with reason 'removed'. Each amendment also leaves a note. Several amendments files may be given, oldest first and one per date, each applied on top of the last and each source keeping its own file's date; `amendments` then lists them in that order. A 'forms' amendment adds English forms to an existing ruling, naming its current target, and an add may list several English forms; each new form becomes one of the ruling's `en` forms and may not belong to another headword.
